analysis.title: GS Duttenhoefer - Duttenhoefer's Daily 05.10.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 73bps to 7723 (+13% ytd) on weaker NFPs (29k vs consensus 90k) and lower Fed hike probability (<20% for October). Nasdaq reached new all-time highs despite higher yields.
US 10yr unchanged at 5.27% and US 30yr mortgage rates are now above 7.3%. OAT/Bund spread is 160bps, the widest since the 2011 eurozone debt crisis.
Brent is back at $102 on Iran headlines. Gold is $4130, Bitcoin $85k, and EUR/USD is below 1.12 for the first time since May 2025. Nvidia market cap touched $5.7tn.

US x Iran: the Pentagon confirmed deployment of a third carrier strike group (USS Theodore Roosevelt) and 10k additional troops to the Persian Gulf. Tehran is preparing a broader response to any renewed large-scale US attack.
Hedge funds: US L/S net leverage fell for a 3rd consecutive week to 46.4%, the lowest since April 2025 and near 5-year lows (2nd percentile). Europe saw its largest % net buying in over five years.
Data center construction spending rose +73.2% y/y in August to $85bn, while total US construction spending fell -1.7% y/y.

Q3 earnings season starts next week. Consensus expects S&P 500 y/y EPS growth of 27% in Q3. AI infrastructure spending accounts for over 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth this quarter, alongside hyperscaler capex growth of 116%. Median S&P stock EPS growth is about 9% in Q3 vs 14% in Q2.

Earnings concentration: the top 10 contributors are expected to account for 68% of aggregate S&P 500 earnings growth in 3Q26 (vs 48% in 2Q26). Micron and Nvidia together account for 34% of index growth.
Fed: GS thinks an October hike is unlikely and sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes additional hikes are unnecessary.

Amazon is a new Conviction List add into Q3. The analyst sees upside from above-Street AWS growth and margins, the orchestration layer, a ~$70bn Physical AI opportunity and digital advertising strength, despite the agentic commerce debate.

Gold: S&P Global identifies only 9 deposits discovered since 2020 that reached its 2m-ounce threshold. The average major find since 2020 holds 4.3m ounces vs 7.3m in the 2010s, and discovery-to-production timelines have stretched to 16 years.
EU Conviction List adds: Solaria, Straumann, Scout24 and IMCD. Removals: Naturgy, Norsk Hydro and Smith & Nephew.

Duration play: the GSXUBOND Index (48 stocks) has RSI below 30 and forward dividend yield above 4%. On the five prior occasions with those conditions, 1-month returns averaged +2.7% with an 80% hit rate and 3-month returns averaged +5.9%. GS frames it as a tactical opportunity or a hedge for a book short duration.

Chip pricing: the GS DRAM sentiment indicator for September points moderately positive. DDR5/DDR4 pricing continued rising, server ODM monthly revenue growth hit a record +130% y/y, and conventional memory and HBM pricing expectations have been reset and started to recover.

EU equities have underperformed other regions since August. Europe has a FCF yield of 5.5% vs 3.5% for the US, buybacks continue, equity supply is net negative and M&A is at highs. GS stays overweight Technology, Banks, Renewables, Defense and Capital intensive.
Breadth: the market is 2% from its all-time high but the median stock is 17% below its high, leaving S&P 500 breadth at its lowest since the Dot Com Bubble.
US-listed ETFs have taken in more than $1.5tn this year, passing last year's record in 3 quarters. GS expects US ETF flows to exceed $2tn in 2026.
